chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Muhammad ibn Hakim from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said:

When you buy a female slave, and her master guarantees to you that she is in a state of ritual purity (free from menstruation or post-partum bleeding), there is no harm in having intercourse with her.

key_terms.طُهْر: Ritual purity (specifically freedom from menstruation/post-partum bleeding in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having intercourse with a newly purchased female slave if the seller guarantees she is pure?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the principle of reliance (tawakkul) on the seller's guarantee regarding a female slave's purity, exempting the buyer from the standard waiting period (istibra') to confirm virginity or freedom from pregnancy. It highlights the Shia juristic view that a specific warranty of purity overrides the general precautionary measure, reflecting the practical legal frameworks of the Abbasid era regarding slave markets. The ruling underscores the importance of contractual assurance in mitigating ritual and legal uncertainties in personal status matters.
